hero.title: PayPal Hosted Buttons
hero.description: The newer paypal.com/sdk/js?components=hosted-buttons / paypal.HostedButtons product. Needs both a client-id and a hosted button ID from the org's own PayPal dashboard — real values only, no safe dummy ID for live rendering (see the gotcha below).

example.title: Example
example.note: This example is intentionally left unconfigured (no `clientId`/`hostedButtonId`) rather than using a dummy ID: unlike the legacy Donate Button, the Hosted Buttons SDK makes a live client-side API call to fetch the button's config, so a fake ID here would surface a real, misleading error instead of safe placeholder documentation.

gotcha.title: Known gotcha
gotcha.text: A wrong or nonexistent `hostedButtonId` surfaces as a browser CORS policy violation (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header on PayPal's `paypal.com/ncp/api/form-fields/<id>` response), not a clear "invalid ID" error — easy to misdiagnose as a domain-whitelist problem. Verify the ID first with the exact literal snippet PayPal's dashboard provides, in a bare static HTML file, before assuming a CORS/whitelist issue.

standard.title: Standard
items: Render `PayPalHostedButton` with real `clientId`/`hostedButtonId` values from `DONATION_METHODS`/donation config — never hardcode them a second time at the call site.
The fallback "having trouble" link uses `https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/<hostedButtonId>` — a different URL shape from the Donate Button product's `paypal.com/donate?hosted_button_id=...`.

The component fills its parent's full width by default (`w-full`) — a PayPal Hosted Buttons widget with no explicit width, inside a `flex`/`items-center` layout, collapses to shrink-wrap width and its own text wraps one letter per line. Cap width with `className` at the call site instead of removing the base `w-full`.
If the client-id or hosted-button-id is missing, the component renders a clearly labeled "not configured" box rather than a blank area or a live API call.
